title: Price chart: shade background regions by historical Screen 1 (Tide) trend
description: The very first idea logged in docs/ideas.md, now unblocked: shade the price chart's background by historical Tide state (bull/bear/neutral) so it's visually obvious when BUY/SELL were even structurally possible vs. gated off entirely by a Neutral or opposite-direction Tide -- directly answers the kind of question this session spent a long time investigating conversationally for ORCL/V ('why did this signal barely ever fire'). lightweight-charts has no native background-band primitive -- use a low-opacity area series or equivalent plugin technique; decide and record. Per the project's established explanatory pattern (common/InfoBalloon, common/MetricHelp, metricHelpContent.ts, signalExplanation.ts, docs/tasks/frontend-stock-detail-metric-help.json), every new visual element this task adds must be explainable, not just displayed: a help affordance (reuse MetricHelp where it fits) that states what the metric/signal is, how it relates to Dr. Elder's methodology, and, where meaningful, an explanation of the CURRENT value shown -- not a static definition alone. Add an entry to metricHelpContent.ts's registry rather than inventing a parallel explanation mechanism.

checklist.step: Decide the rendering technique (low-opacity area series vs. a plugin) given lightweight-charts has no native background-band primitive; record as a decisions entry.
Implement the shading using the newly-exposed tide_trend per historical bar (backend-indicator-history-tide-exposure).
Add a legend/key so the three colors (or equivalent) are self-explanatory, plus a MetricHelp entry explaining what Tide/Screen 1 means and why it gates everything else.
Verify visually against a real ticker with a known Tide history (e.g. ORCL or V from this session's own conversation) that the shading correctly matches known BULLISH/BEARISH/NEUTRAL stretches.
Tests + Storybook story if a new common/ piece was introduced; confirm 90% coverage gate holds.

decisions.decision: Render the background shading as one lightweight-charts AreaSeries PER CONTIGUOUS same-trend segment (not one long-lived series per trend, and not a custom series plugin), each pinned to its own dedicated, invisible [0,1] priceScaleId (`tide-region-shading`) with a fixed autoscaleInfoProvider so it can never influence or be distorted by the real candlestick price scale.
decisions.rationale: Considered and rejected two alternatives during a live-browser verification pass against real cached ORCL/V data (docs/tasks index -> backend-indicator-history-tide-exposure dependency already merged): (1) a single huge-value AreaSeries per trend on the chart's own real price scale with autoscaleInfoProvider returning null to exclude it -- rejected because the huge value's pixel mapping still depends on the real scale's current bounds, and because a live browser test proved lightweight-charts' AreaSeries fill BRIDGES STRAIGHT ACROSS any gap between two of a series' own real points -- real omission or an explicit WhitespaceData point alike -- so a single series per trend (bullish/bearish/neutral) rendered three giant overlapping blobs, each spanning from that trend's first occurrence in the visible range to its last, with whichever trend's series was added most recently painting over the other two. This was caught only via a real browser screenshot against ORCL/V's actual Tide history (mocked unit tests never exercised more than one gap in a trend's own array, so never caught it) -- a small purpose-built standalone HTML page loading the real lightweight-charts package confirmed the bridging behavior conclusively. (2) a custom series plugin (ICustomSeriesPaneView) -- rejected as overkill complexity for a decorative background band when the private-price-scale + one-series-per-bounded-span technique (the same 'one series per bounded span' pattern buildZoneRenderData already established for support/resistance zone bands) works and is simpler. Each segment's own data is extended with one trailing point at the NEXT segment's own start date so even a single-bar segment (a real, common case for a brief Tide flip) renders as a real 2-point filled span with actual width rather than an invisible lone point.

decisions.decision: Two further real integration bugs found only via a live browser walkthrough (not the mocked unit tests) and fixed: (a) chart.priceScale(id).applyOptions(...) must be called AFTER at least one series with that priceScaleId has been added -- calling it before throws synchronously ('Trying to apply price scale options with incorrect ID'), so the code now configures the scale via series.priceScale().applyOptions(...) on one of the already-added region series instead. (b) The three/N region series were given no plain `title`, and `lineColor` is set explicitly to each segment's own trend color -- omitting `title` avoids a `lastValueVisible:false`-independent 'Tide: Bullish'-style label badge Lightweight Charts still renders next to the (hidden) last-value label, and setting `lineColor` avoids that badge defaulting to the library's own hardcoded green (#33D778) fallback when unset.
decisions.rationale: Both bugs were invisible to the existing mocked-lightweight-charts unit tests (the test double has no equivalent validation/default-fallback behavior), and were only caught by actually running the app (make backend + make frontend) against the real, already-cached ORCL/V daily/weekly OHLCV in backend/fintrade.db (bumping the 24h-TTL cache rows' fetched_at forward so the CachedDataProvider served them without a live network call, per docs/architecture/Backend.md §7) and taking real Playwright screenshots. Fixing both before merge was judged necessary since either would have shipped a broken or visually-cluttered feature despite all existing/added unit tests passing -- this task's own checklist item 4 (visual verification against real ORCL/V Tide history) existed specifically to catch exactly this class of gap.

decisions.decision: Reused the existing theme.palette.signal.buy/sell/hold colors (green/red/amber) for Bullish/Bearish/Neutral shading rather than adding new dedicated 'tide' palette keys the way divergence/season/kangarooTail each did.
decisions.rationale: Tide Bullish/Bearish/Neutral maps semantically onto the same BUY-only/SELL-only/neither-allowed meaning the signal palette already carries elsewhere on this exact page (BUY/SELL/HOLD badges, transition markers) -- Screen 1 literally gates which of BUY/SELL is even considered, so reusing signal.buy/sell/hold reinforces that connection rather than introducing a fourth, unrelated color system a viewer would have to learn. Fill alpha (~8%, TIDE_REGION_FILL_ALPHA) is deliberately much fainter than the value-zone (~20%) or support/resistance zone (7%-29%) shadings, since this shading covers the ENTIRE pane behind every other overlay rather than a bounded slice of the price range.

decisions.decision: Added the shading as its own SEPARATE `useEffect` (not folded into the existing EMA/channel/value-zone/marker signal-overlay effect), even though both share identical gating (`overlayEnabled`, `indicatorsQuery.data`, `historyQuery.data`, `theme`).
decisions.rationale: Matches this component's own established convention of isolating each independently-reasoned-about overlay into its own effect (support/resistance zones, divergence, kangaroo tail are all already separate effects despite some sharing gating/data sources with each other) -- keeps the large, delicate signal-overlay effect's own carefully-ordered cleanup (documented at length in its own comment, including a previously-shipped crash) untouched and independently testable, and keeps this new effect's own cleanup/dependency footprint easy to reason about in isolation.

decisions.decision: Added a new `tideRegionHelp` entry to metricHelpContent.ts (reusing the existing common/MetricHelp affordance) rather than reusing the pre-existing `tideHelp` entry (ScreensPanel.tsx's latest-value-only Tide panel).
decisions.rationale: `tideHelp` explains only TODAY's Tide reading; this task's own explicit ask ('why did a BUY/SELL barely fire' -- the motivating ORCL/V investigation) needed the explanation to describe the CURRENT (windowed) chart's actual historical composition, not just today's single value. `tideRegionHelp.interpretValue` computes the Bullish/Bearish/Neutral percentage split from the exact same `selectVisibleIndicatorPoints`-windowed dataset the chart-drawing effect itself draws from (shared, not independently recomputed), so the legend text can never describe a different set of bars than what's actually shaded -- the same data-source-consistency convention this task's own context note calls out (the PR #152 round-2 legend/chart mismatch bug class).

decisions.decision: No new common/ component and no new Storybook story: the legend row reuses the existing common/MetricHelp affordance (same pattern as every other PriceChart.tsx overlay legend), not a new reusable component.
decisions.rationale: Per Frontend.md's common/-vs-feature-specific placement test, a new common/ piece is only warranted when introducing new *reusable* UI, not a new usage of an existing one -- the swatches are plain inline Box/Typography, matching every other legend row on this exact chart.
